issues.legal_issue: A confirmed public-auction sale supported by a sale certificate gives the purchaser title that cannot be displaced unless the sale is set aside through the prescribed procedure.
material_facts: A purchaser paid the accepted highest bid for the land at a public auction conducted to dispose of property in the compensation pool.
The sale was confirmed and a sale certificate was issued, with effect from the date of confirmation.
No application to set aside the auction sale was shown, and the authorised officer had not set aside the sale on its own motion.
The sale certificate was issued while proceedings concerning a competing allotment claim were still ongoing.
issues.conclusion: The purchaser obtained title on confirmation of the sale, and the land could not later be dealt with as compensation-pool property while that sale remained in force.
issues.legal_principle: Under Rules 34H, 90(15), and 92 of the Displaced Persons Compensation and Rehabilitation Rules, 1955, property not allotted under Chapter V may be sold under Chapter XIV, a sale certificate is issued after sale, and a sale may be set aside only through the prescribed procedure. Under Bishan Paul v. Mothu Ram, title passes upon confirmation of the sale and the certificate relates back to that date. In the absence of a valid setting aside, the sale remains effective.

rule.if: compensation_pool_sale_appeal and public_auction_purchase_confirmed and purchase_price_paid and sale_certificate_issued and sale_not_set_aside_through_prescribed_procedure

predicates.compensation_pool_sale_appeal: The proceeding concerns an appeal about a sale of property held in a compensation pool.
predicates.public_auction_purchase_confirmed: A public auction purchaser's bid was accepted and the sale was confirmed by the competent authority.
predicates.purchase_price_paid: The auction purchaser paid the accepted purchase price.
predicates.sale_certificate_issued: The authority issued a sale certificate to the auction purchaser.
predicates.sale_not_set_aside_through_prescribed_pr: No competent authority set aside the sale through the procedure provided for doing so.

issues.definition: When a compensation-pool sale has been confirmed, paid for, and certified, and has not been set aside through the prescribed procedure, the purchaser retains title.

issues.legal_issue: A civil decree declaring possession in a dispute between private persons cannot collaterally invalidate a statutory auction sale when the sale and its authorities were not challenged in that suit.
material_facts: The claimant brought a civil suit against the former lessee seeking a declaration of continuous possession.
Neither the auction purchaser nor the rehabilitation authority was a party to that suit.
The suit did not challenge an order made under the governing statutory scheme concerning the auction sale.
No finding was shown that the sale authority had failed to comply with the statute or fundamental principles of judicial procedure.
issues.conclusion: The civil decree could not collaterally affect or invalidate the auction sale, even if the decree was not collusive.
issues.legal_principle: Section 27 of the Displaced Persons Compensation and Rehabilitation Act, 1954 makes orders under the Act final, subject to the established limits on excluding civil-court jurisdiction. Under section 9 of the Code of Civil Procedure, and Secretary of State v. Mask and Co. and State of Kerala v. M/s. N. Ramaswami Iyer and Sons, a civil court may intervene where statutory provisions have not been complied with or a statutory tribunal has violated fundamental principles of judicial procedure. A decree in a possession suit that does not challenge the statutory sale does not itself set that sale aside.

predicates.statutory_auction_sale_dispute: The proceeding concerns whether a statutory auction sale remains effective.
predicates.civil_suit_declares_possession_against_p: A claimant obtained a civil decree declaring possession in a suit against a private person connected with the land.
predicates.sale_authority_and_purchaser_not_parties: Neither the authority that conducted the sale nor the purchaser was a party to the civil suit.
predicates.no_finding_of_statutory_or_procedural_vi: The civil proceedings did not establish that the statutory authority failed to comply with the governing law or fundamental principles of judicial procedure.

issues.definition: A possession decree in a suit against a private person, where the sale authority and purchaser were absent and no statutory or procedural violation was established, cannot invalidate the auction sale.

issues.legal_issue: When state action creates competing equities between a bona fide auction purchaser and a claimant with a sustained allotment claim, the land may be divided equally to do justice between them.
material_facts: A displaced person bought the land in good faith at a public auction, paid the purchase price, and received a sale certificate.

A competing displaced-person claimant had been inducted as a sub-lessee and remained in possession of the land; records supported possession during relevant periods, and missing or illegible records were treated as insufficient to defeat continuity.
The state confirmed the auction sale and issued the sale certificate without waiting for the final outcome of the competing allotment proceedings.
The purchaser was deprived of the land's use while the claimant remained in possession, and both parties were involved in prolonged litigation.
The land was limited and had become scarce and more valuable, and the court considered that each claimant had a substantial equitable claim.
issues.conclusion: The impugned orders were set aside, and the land was ordered to be divided into two equal halves, with one half delivered to the auction purchaser and the other allotted to the claimant under Rule 34C.
issues.legal_principle: Rule 34C of the Displaced Persons Compensation and Rehabilitation Rules, 1955 provides for allotment to a qualifying sub-lessee in continuous occupation, while Rule 34H provides for disposal of land not allotted under Chapter V. Where administrative handling creates competing equities that cannot fairly be resolved by enforcing only one claim, the Court may apply equitable and distributive justice to provide relief to both parties. The Court discussed the ideas of justice and equity associated with Justinian, Aristotle, Radbruch, and Cardozo.

rule.if: civil_appeal_over_competing_land_claims and purchaser_bought_in_good_faith_and_paid and claimant_maintained_sublease_possession and state_finalized_sale_before_allotment_claim_was_resolved and both_claimants_suffered_prolonged_litigation and land_is_limited

predicates.civil_appeal_over_competing_land_claims: The proceeding is an appeal concerning competing claims to the same land by an auction purchaser and an allotment claimant.
predicates.purchaser_bought_in_good_faith_and_paid: The purchaser bought the land in good faith at public auction and paid the purchase price.
predicates.claimant_maintained_sublease_possession: The allotment claimant had been inducted as a sub-lessee and remained in possession of the land.
predicates.state_finalized_sale_before_allotment_cl: The state confirmed the sale or issued its certificate before the competing allotment proceedings had finally concluded.
predicates.both_claimants_suffered_prolonged_litiga: Both claimants were subjected to prolonged litigation over their competing claims.
predicates.land_is_limited: The land available to satisfy the competing claims was limited.

issues.definition: When a good-faith paid purchaser and a claimant who remained in sublease possession have competing claims, state action finalized the sale before the allotment claim was resolved, both endured prolonged litigation, and land is limited, the land is divided equally between them.
